title: POC kickoff & timeline - Nova Insurance
summary: Kickoff for a 6-week POC to validate Redwood inference for insurance claims triage. Covered success criteria (latency, accuracy on sample prompts, cost targets), workload sizing (peak/steady qps, average token lengths), bench plan (latency & throughput on hosted vs dedicated, quantized models), and milestones (kickoff, infra access, mid-point review, executive readout). Decided next steps: Redwood to share formal POC proposal, benchmark plan, and temporary access checklist; customer to share sample prompt sets, data residency requirements, and scheduling for mid-point exec slot.
next_steps: Alex: Send POC proposal + pricing breakdown by 2025-12-09
Maya: Share sample prompt sets and 2 weeks of anonymized logs by 2025-12-12
Priya: Draft benchmark plan and test matrix by 2025-12-10
Liam: Provision network access or provide firewall rules by 2025-12-11
action_items: Alex Chen: Prepare POC statement of work and pricing - due 2025-12-09
Priya Kapoor: Benchmark test matrix + runbook - due 2025-12-10
Maya Rodriguez: Provide sample prompts and anonymized logs - due 2025-12-12
Liam O'Connor: Provide VPC peering details or NAT rules - due 2025-12-11
transcript:
Header: 2025-12-05 14:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Kapoor, Diego Martinez (Redwood); Maya Rodriguez, Liam O'Connor, Sofia Alvarez, Ravi Patel (Nova Insurance)

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Alex from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. Priya and Diego from our SE team are on as well. Quick roll call?
[00:10] Maya Rodriguez: Hi Maya here.
[00:12] Liam O'Connor: Liam.
[00:14] Sofia Alvarez: Sofia.
[00:16] Ravi Patel: Ravi.
[00:18] Priya Kapoor: Great, thanks. Agenda: scoping the POC, clarify success criteria, figure out workload sizing and benchmark plan, and outline timeline/milestones.
[00:30] Maya Rodriguez: High level we want to validate Redwood for our claims triage workflow. Key thing is latency under load and that the model matches our business accuracy thresholds. Also data residency and audit logs are must-haves.
[00:45] Priya Kapoor: Understood. When you say "business accuracy" can you give an example or pass a threshold?
[00:50] Maya Rodriguez: Sure, for the classification prompts we want >= 92% agreement with our human labels on a 3k eval set, and false negative rate under 4% for high-risk claims. Those would be POC success criteria.
[01:06] Diego Martinez: Helpful. On latency, what's your SLO? P50/P95 targets?
[01:12] Ravi Patel: We want median under 400ms and P95 under 900ms for single-turn classification with avg token length about 120 tokens. Under batch scoring during peak we'd accept higher but prefer under 2s.
[01:26] Priya Kapoor: That maps cleanly to what we can test: single-request latency and sustained throughput. We'll include both hosted and dedicated variants in the bench to show tradeoffs - quantized model variants often reduce cost but may affect accuracy slightly.
[01:40] Liam O'Connor: Speaking of cost, curious on ballpark numbers for per-1M tokens for hosted vs dedicated - and how caching/prefixing might reduce cost.
[01:48] Alex Chen: We'll include a pricing appendix. Quick note: Redwood Optimize will recommend batching/caching settings tailored to your workload; the POC will include a run to show potential savings.
[02:05] Sofia Alvarez: On security, we need SOC2 type II evidence, SAML SSO, KMS integration for key management, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Also we likely need a VPC peering or private link for the dedicated environment.
[02:20] Diego Martinez: Yep we can support VPC peering and customer-managed KMS. We'll list the exact network requirements in the access checklist.
[02:30] Maya Rodriguez: Great. For benchmarking data we'll share a sample of anonymized logs. Is 2 weeks of traffic enough?
[02:38] Priya Kapoor: 2 weeks is perfect to capture burst patterns. We'll ask for a small eval set (~3k labelled examples) plus 2 weeks of logs for sizing.
[02:50] Ravi Patel: How long do you expect the whole POC to be?
[02:53] Alex Chen: We're proposing a 6-week POC: Week 0-1 kickoff and access setup; Week 2 run initial bench on hosted; Week 3-4 run dedicated + tuning and midpoint review; Week 5 final run + exec readout in week 6.
[03:10] Maya Rodriguez: OK timeline seems reasonable. Can we lock a mid-point exec slot now? We need to coordinate with our execs.
[03:16] Ravi Patel: I can tentatively block 2026-01-14 for a mid-point review, pending confirmation.
[03:22] Priya Kapoor: Noted. We'll keep that tentative. Mid-point review will include results vs success criteria, a demo of the pipeline, and proposed next steps for production.
[03:36] Liam O'Connor: About access, we prefer VPC peering; if that takes longer can we start with a safe hosted test and then move to dedicated once network is ready?
[03:45] Diego Martinez: Absolutely. We'll run early benches on hosted with synthetic traffic and your logs, and then re-run on dedicated once access's in place - that'll also show the variance due to quantization and kernel selection.
[04:00] Maya Rodriguez: For acceptance, what do you need from product teams?
[04:03] Alex Chen: Ideally: samples, logs, security contacts for the network setup, and a decision-maker for the final exec readout. Also, sign-off on the SOW.
[04:12] Maya Rodriguez: I'll be the business owner, Ravi will coordinate infra, Sofia will own security sign-off.
[04:18] Priya Kapoor: Bench plan - we'll run latency P50/P95 per model variant, throughput until 90% GPU utilization, token cost per 1k tokens, and regression checks against your labeled eval set. We'll also include a small adversarial prompt set to test edge cases.
[04:36] Liam O'Connor: When you say "model variants", which ones will you test?
[04:39] Priya Kapoor: We'll pick two open models from the catalog tuned for instruction-following, plus a quantized 4-bit variant. We'll compare hosted baseline, dedicated baseline (same FP16), and quantized dedicated. If you want we can also include a smaller low-latency model for fast path.
[04:55] Maya Rodriguez: Please include a baseline run against our current setup (we use a mix of in-house embeddings + rules). We need a like-for-like comparison.
[05:02] Diego Martinez: We'll add a "current baseline" section - please send a short doc about your current stack.
[05:09] Ravi Patel: Any legal steps required?
[05:11] Alex Chen: We'll attach our standard POC MSA and data addendum; legal will do a quick review. For security docs, we'll send our SOC2 report and technical security pack.
[05:22] Sofia Alvarez: We need encryption-in-transit and at-rest confirmation plus RSA for sys logs, and a KMS flow diagram.
[05:28] Diego Martinez: We'll include a KMS integration diagram in the access checklist.
[05:32] Maya Rodriguez: Good. What are success/failure gates for this trial?
[05:35] Priya Kapoor: Success: >=92% accuracy on the labeled set AND median latency <400ms on single-turn tests AND operational checklist completed (VPC or approved hosted controls). Failure would be not meeting any of the primary thresholds after reasonable tuning. We'll also mark partial success if we meet accuracy but need more infra for latency.
[05:55] Alex Chen: Okay to recap milestones: Kickoff & access setup (this week - week 1), initial hosted benchmarks (week 2), dedicated benchmarking + tuning (weeks 3-4), mid-point review (week 4), final runs & exec readout (weeks 5-6). We'll circulate a calendar invite for the mid-point tentative date.
[06:12] Maya Rodriguez: Sounds good. Can you send the POC SOW and benchmark plan?
[06:16] Alex Chen: Yes - action item: Alex to send SOW + pricing by 2025-12-09, Priya to send bench plan by 2025-12-10.
[06:24] Ravi Patel: I'll start the internal tickets for network.
[06:26] Liam O'Connor: I'll share firewall/ip list and a sample of anonymized logs.
[06:30] Sofia Alvarez: I'll review security docs when you send them and follow up with a set of questions.
[06:35] Priya Kapoor: Any other open questions?
[06:37] Maya Rodriguez: Not from me.
[06:38] Alex Chen: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up over email and Slack.
[06:42] End of call.

References mentioned: POC proposal (link: /redwood/poc-proposal-nova.pdf), Benchmark plan (link: /redwood/benchmarks/nova-bench-plan.xlsx), Security pack (link: /redwood/security/soc2.pdf). Note: transcript contains some auto-caption noise and occasional mis-attributions.
